title: iSWAP maximises the second-moment spectral gap in random quantum circuits
abstract: We prove that the $\mathrm{iSWAP}$ gate maximises the spectral gap of the Hermitian second-moment operator on every connected graph with at least three vertices, among all two-local unitary circuit ensembles. We further prove that the polyhedral cone defined by asymmetric four-point inequalities is invariant under the transpose of the $\mathrm{iSWAP}$ semigroup, yielding a componentwise comparison certificate for its positive Perron--Frobenius eigenvector. These results resolve a conjecture of Kong, Li, and Liu.
summary: The paper rigorously proves that using the iSWAP gate maximizes the spectral gap of the second-moment operator in random quantum circuits defined on any connected graph. It achieves this by employing sophisticated mathematical tools like Perron–Frobenius theory to compare the dynamics generated by arbitrary local gates against those generated by iSWAP.
main_problem: The research aims to determine which two-local unitary gate ensemble maximizes the spectral gap of the Hermitian second-moment operator for random quantum circuits on a given graph.
main_result: The iSWAP gate was proven to maximize this spectral gap among all considered two-local circuit ensembles for connected graphs with at least three vertices.
method: The proof involves advanced mathematical techniques, including analyzing the invariance of polyhedral cones under the iSWAP semigroup and utilizing Perron–Frobenius theory on associated block matrices.
model_or_system: The model consists of random quantum circuits applied to a connected graph G=(V, E), where the dynamics are governed by local two-qubit unitaries acting on edges. The analysis focuses on the second-moment operator derived from these gates.
key_observables: Spectral gap ($\Delta(T)$) of the second-moment operator; largest non-trivial eigenvalue ($\lambda^\star$) and minimum eigenvalue ($\mu_3$).
important_parameters: The graph structure (connectedness, $|V| \ge 3$); parameters $(\alpha,  eta)$ characterizing local gate strengths.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the resulting average moment operator is Hermitian; comparisons are often reduced to analyzing specific boundary conditions or parameter regimes.

It then reduces this comparison to analyzing specific mathematical objects (cones, block matrices) whose properties are proven using Perron–Frobenius theory, culminating in the main theorem comparing iSWAP to arbitrary ensembles.
